title: Feeling Your Feet on the Ground
description: For the moments when everything speeds up and you feel far away from yourself. Each day teaches one simple grounding practice, so you have a toolkit ready when you need to come back to the present.
tasks: Press your feet into the floor and feel the ground push back, for thirty seconds.
Name five things you can see, four you can hear, three you can touch, two you can smell, and one you can taste.
Hold a piece of ice or run cold water over your wrists for one minute.
Breathe in for four, hold for four, out for four, hold for four. Repeat four times.
Describe the room you are in out loud, in detail, as if to someone who cannot see it.
Walk barefoot on grass, sand, or your floor for two minutes and notice every step.
Squeeze each muscle group for five seconds, then release, from your feet to your face.
Carry a small object in your pocket today, a stone, a coin, a shell, and touch it when you need to.
Name every color you can see from where you are sitting.
Sit with your back against a wall and feel the support behind you for one minute.
Count backward from fifty by threes.
Drink something cold or warm slowly, noticing the temperature travel down.
Name three things that are true right now: the date, where you are, what you are doing.
Hum a steady note for thirty seconds and feel the vibration in your chest.
Wrap yourself in a blanket or put on a heavy coat for five minutes and feel the weight.
Trace the outline of your hand with a finger, breathing in up each finger and out down the other side.
Smell something strong and pleasant: coffee, citrus, mint, soap.
Stamp your feet or clap your hands for twenty seconds.
Look at something far away, then something close, and switch five times.
Say your full name, your age, and today's date out loud.
Push against a wall with both hands as hard as you can for ten seconds. Then rest.
List five things in the room that are the same color, then five that are round.
Rub your palms together until they are warm and place them over your eyes.
Notice the weight of your body on the chair, the bed, or the ground, for one minute.
Eat something with a strong taste slowly: a mint, a lemon slice, a pickle.
Walk up and down a flight of stairs, counting each step out loud.
Hold a warm mug with both hands and feel the heat spread into your fingers.
Draw or write your name with your non-dominant hand.
Pick a category, animals, cities, foods, and name one for each letter of the alphabet.
Write down the three grounding practices from this challenge that worked best for you. Keep the list somewhere you can find it fast.
Stand in a doorway and press your palms outward against both sides of the frame for ten seconds, then let your arms drop and notice the difference.
Put one hand flat on your desk and describe its surface silently: cool or warm, smooth or rough, hard or giving.
Run your fingertips along the seam of your jeans or the edge of your sleeve and follow every stitch you can feel.
Sit in your parked car before you drive and feel the steering wheel under both hands for three slow breaths.
Take off your shoes at home and press each toe into the floor one at a time, from the big toe to the little one.
Listen for the farthest sound you can hear, then the nearest, and name them both.
Hold a cold glass of water against the inside of one wrist for twenty seconds, then the other.
Open a window or step outside and feel the air on your face, noting whether it is cooler or warmer than the room.
Roll your shoulders back five times slowly and feel your shoulder blades slide across your back.
Place both feet flat on the floor at your desk and count how many points of contact your body has with the chair.
Peel an orange or a clementine slowly and let the smell fill the space around you.
In a waiting room, find every rectangle you can see and count them quietly.
Lie on your bed and let it hold your full weight, letting each limb go heavy one at a time.
Chew a piece of gum and pay attention to the flavor as it fades over one minute.
Stand on one foot for as long as you comfortably can, then switch, and notice how your ankle works to keep you upright.
Press the tip of your tongue to the roof of your mouth and hold it there for five breaths.
Find a wall, a tree, or a post and lean your whole back against it until you feel steady.
Grip the edge of a table and pull gently toward you for ten seconds, feeling the muscles in your forearms.
Splash cool water on your face and pat it dry, noticing the change on your skin.
Trace the letters of a word you can see, a sign, a label, a book spine, with your eyes, one letter at a time.
Hold your phone or keys and notice their exact weight in your palm, then set them down and notice the absence.

Hold a spoon from the drawer and feel the metal warm up to your hand.
Press your thumb into the center of your opposite palm and hold for ten seconds, then swap hands.
Name the texture of five things within arm's reach without touching them, then touch them and see if you were right.

Tap each fingertip against your thumb in order, then backward, ten times through.

Put on a pair of thick socks and notice how your feet feel different for the next five minutes.
Hold a book with both hands and feel its exact weight, then open it and smell the pages.

Hold a leaf, a blade of grass, or a flower petal and study its veins up close.

Press your fingertips together one pair at a time and hold each for a count of three.
Find the coolest surface in the room and rest your forearm on it for a minute.
